title: UMich, PSI researchers report new airborne radiation-detection method
summary: Researchers from the University of Michigan College of Engineering and Switzerland’s Paul Scherrer Institute are reporting the development of a new airborne method of radiation detection that accurately identifies single or mixed source identity, activity, and location. Their research has been published in Nature Communications under the title “Quantitative Mobile Gamma-Ray Spectrometry through Bayesian Inference.” The research is expected to improve the work of emergency responders by enabling them to more quickly and precisely determine where people in radiologically hazardous situations—such as a nuclear reactor meltdown or a nuclear weapon detonation—should evacuate for safe shelter. The research also should help responders better determine what other types of protective measures should be implemented for such people, including distribution of protective equipment and potassium iodide pills (which protect the thyroid gland from radiation).

title: New Polling Reveals Majority Of Australians Support Nuclear Energy
summary: Almost two-thirds of Australians believe nuclear power should be part of the nation's energy future, as new polling reveals growing concerns about Australia's ability to meet its electricity needs. New YouGov research commissioned by lobby group Nuclear for Australia has found that 63% of Australians believe nuclear power should be considered, while 60% believe it will form part of Australia’s future energy mix. The findings come as both the demand for and cost of electricity grows, driven by AI, data centres and electrification, while the conflict in the Middle East contributes to uncertainty in global energy markets.

title: Nucleon Fuel seeks $20M grant for Wyo. conversion facility
summary: Nucleon Fuel, a subsidiary of Canadian small modular reactor developer Nucleon Energy, has applied for a $20 million grant and possible $10 million additional loan to build a uranium conversion facility near Gillette, Wyo. Both the grant and the loan would be funded by Wyoming’s recently created Energy Dominance Fund, which seeks to advance projects related to oil, natural gas, coal, and nuclear energy in the state.

title: Integrated Repository For Slovenia’s Krško Plant And Test Reactor ‘Cheaper Than Standalone Site’
summary: Integrating a deep geologic repository for spent nuclear fuel from Slovenia’s Triga II research reactor into a site at the country’s Krško nuclear power plant would be cheaper than creating a standalone site, a study has shown. The study was carried out by Slovenia’s Agency for Radioactive Waste Management (Arao) and US-based Deep Isolation, which is developing nuclear waste disposal technologies in deep boreholes. The results showed that co-locating spent fuel from the Triga II reactor, which is at the Jožef Stefan Institute near the Slovenian capital of Ljubljana, would avoid duplicating costs over a standalone repository, which would require independent siting and licensing.

title: Hands Off the Glovebox: An Electrochemical System for Semiautonomous Decontamination at Los Alamos
summary: The radiological glovebox is among the most recognizable pieces of contaminated infrastructure in the nuclear enterprise, and among the most difficult for disposition. Every glovebox used in plutonium operations eventually reaches the end of its service life. It can be dispositioned in its contaminated state, but at considerable cost: disposal as transuranic (TRU) waste is orders of magnitude more expensive than disposal as low-level waste, and it consumes limited capacity at the Waste Isolation Pilot Plant in Carlsbad, N.M., the nation’s only deep geologic repository for defense TRU waste. This economic reality makes decontamination to LLW limits the strongly preferred disposition path. Today, that work is typically performed by an operator reaching through glove ports to repeatedly spray and wipe interior surfaces until surveys confirm acceptable contamination levels. The process is slow, physically demanding, and dose-intensive, and the wipes, rags, and spent reagents it consumes become radioactive waste themselves.
